then.text: Wad clay all used up? Good. That's what it's for.
Wad clay for the bungs? Here, a good soft roll. Squash it between the saggars and it seals the joints, so the smoke can't get in and spoil the glaze.
Bone china's a different beast. Cornish china clay, china stone and ground-up cattle bone, about half and half. Spode got the mix right around 1800.

else.text: Clay cellar. Cold, damp and very, very brown. Perfect conditions. For clay. Not for people.

blue_italian.text: Spode's Blue Italian. An Italian landscape, a ruined castle, cows having a paddle. It's been made since 1816.
My nan had it, my mum had it, I have it. One day somebody will inherit forty-two side plates and wonder why.
